question: A teacher claims: “If you move an electron farther from a proton, gravity might eventually overtake the electric force.” For two stationary point charges—a proton and an electron—in vacuum, evaluate the accuracy of this claim with reason.

options.A: True, because gravitational force decreases more slowly with distance than electric force.
options.B: False, because for stationary point charges in vacuum both forces vary as 1/r², so their ratio is independent of distance and the electric attraction remains enormously larger.
options.C: True only beyond a certain very large distance where fields ‘thin out’.
options.D: Indeterminate without knowing the exact separation.
